habit_scope: Hang then tape gypsum board on 2-story light-wood. CMHC Ch21. 1/2 in common. P08 already names 1/2 in GWB in IRC bracing lengths and under enclosed stairs — this phase is hang and finish.
how_it_is_done: After insulation/air-barrier inspection (Ch2 Interior Finishes: ceiling, wall and floor finishes). Can overlap cladding (P11). No lag days invented.

1/2 in (12.7 mm) gypsum is more commonly used; required when supports are 24 in OC or when the board supports insulation. 3/8 in allowed on walls at 16 in OC when perpendicular to framing. Ceilings: long dimension at right angles to trusses/joists, or parallel if 1x4 strapping. Walls: commonly horizontal so joints sit at a convenient height. Ends on a support, terminate at a corner.

Nails: ringed, 2.3 mm (3/32 in) shanks, 5.5 mm (7/32 in) heads; penetrate ≥20 mm (3/4 in) into wood. Screws: penetrate ≥15 mm (5/8 in). Heads slightly below the paper (dimple) without breaking the paper. Recessed-edge fasteners may sit flush (covered by tape).

Single-nail: ceiling ≤180 mm (7 in) OC; walls ≤200 mm (8 in) OC. Double-nail: pairs 50 mm (2 in) apart, ≤300 mm (12 in) OC on ceilings and walls. Braced-wall high wind/earthquake: nails ≤200 mm (8 in); screws ≤300 mm (12 in). Screws often 300 mm (12 in) OC edges and field; 400 mm (16 in) on walls when supports ≤16 in OC.
Two layers (sound/fire): second-layer fasteners penetrate as much as the first. Resilient channel: channel to structure, board to channel.

Tape at ≥10°C (50°F). Fill joints >3 mm (1/8 in) first. Metal corner bead on externals; folded paper tape on insides. Three coats: 125 mm (5 in) with tape; then 200 mm (8 in) recessed / 250 mm (10 in) unrecessed; then 250–300 mm (10–12 in) recessed / 400 mm (16 in) unrecessed. Light sand. Nail/screw heads: two coats. Popping: use lumber ≤19% MC (NBC) and fasteners just long enough.
Wet areas: water-resistant board; porcelain at showers over moisture-resistant backing; tub/shower joint caulk to CGSB 19.22 (Canadian standard — confirm AHJ).

Float the ceiling at interior partitions. AF&PA: unattached at least 18 in when trusses run perpendicular to the partition (Fig 73). HUD: 16–24 in; 2x blocking as a backer; do not screw the ceiling to that blocking. Keep both.
tools_equipment: Named: screw gun; trowel / wide-blade putty knife; corner bead. Not a SKU list.
inspection_hold_points: 1/2 in when the board supports insulation or at 24 in OC (Ch21).
Nail 3/4 in into wood; screw 5/8 in into wood.
Enclosed stairs already require 1/2 in under-stair (P08 Glencoe) — do not skip that board.
material_classes: 3/8 in gypsum board CLASS (16 in walls only)
typical_duration_sfr: CMHC Ch2 interior finishes about two weeks including floors/doors — not a drywall-only cycle. No lag days invented.
when_this_is_a_bad_idea: Hanging before the insulation inspection. Breaking the paper with over-driven fasteners. 3/8 in ceilings.
why_tier1_never_learned_it: They hang rock. What they skip is 3/4 in nail penetration, dimple without breaking paper, and tape at 50°F.
permit_gate: fire/wet-area board on drawings where required
permit_gate_notes: CMHC Canadian. Confirm AHJ. Do not invent IRC R-numbers. P08 GWB bracing factor is already filed.
risk_if_swapped_late: Changing thickness after hang is a rehang. Catch before the truck.
plain_language_summary: Hang 1/2-inch rock, ceilings first across the joists, walls often sideways. Ring nails 3/4 inch into the wood, or screws 5/8 inch. Dimple, do not blow the paper. Tape three coats, not below 50°F.
spanish_summary: Cuelgue roca de 1/2, techos primero a traves de los joists, paredes a menudo horizontales. Clavos de anillo 3/4 en la madera, o tornillos 5/8. Dimple, no rompa el papel. Cinta a tres capas, no bajo 50°F.
locators: CMHC Ch21 Figs 164–165 — single/double nail, screw OC, three-coat tape
confidence_notes: Nail/screw penetration and OC printed. Canadian NBC labeled. 19% MC is NBC.

fastener_schedule.oc: 7 in ceiling / 8 in wall single; 12 in double
